cognate: *médʰu in all branches (Russ. мёд, Latv. medus, Lith. medus, Gk μέθυ, OE medu, Ved. mádhu); adjective *swéh₂dú- exact in Gk ἡδύ, OE swēte, Ved. svādú-
drift_or_renewal: Balto-Slavic renews the adjective with *sald- (Russ. сладкий, Latv. salds, Lith. saldus; originally 'salted'), having lost *swéh₂du- 'sweet'; Gk μέθυ has drifted from 'mead' to 'wine'
shared_syntax: noun + attributive 'sweet' as a fixed epithet of the drink (Russ. мёд сладкий, Gk μέθυ ἡδύ line-final, OE swētne medo, Ved. svā́du ... mádhu); object of drinking/serving verbs
context: heroic feast and drinking: the bogatyr drains a aurochs-horn (турей рог) or cup of sweet mead; Homeric companions feast on meat and sweet μέθυ; Finnsburh retainers repay the lord's sweet mead; Vedic praise of the sweet honied drink. The Latvian anchor is a love daina using 'sweetness of honey' figuratively, so it carries the BSl. renewal but is the weaker anchor
phrase: *swéh₂du médʰu 'sweet mead' (Russ. мёд сладкий ~ Gk μέθυ ἡδύ ~ OE swētne medo ~ Ved. svādú mádhu)
note: 'Sweet' + 'mead/honey' is natural and the byliny are late; what argues for a formula is the fixed-epithet use in heroic drinking scenes in four branches with exact cognates in three (Gk, Gmc, Indic) and a systematic BSl. renewal. Russian anchors are one stock bylina line repeated; count them as one witness.

cognate: Serb. род ~ Latv. rads 'kinsman' (Balto-Slavic); Serb. мати, gen. матере ~ Latv. māte, gen. mātes < *méh₂tēr
shared_syntax: kin-noun + genitive of 'mother' ('mother's kin'); Serbian formula у род у матере (to her natal kin, at her mother's)
context: a married woman and her natal family: in Vuk the wife flees, or is sent, back у род у матере (a fixed line in at least nine songs); in the Latvian wedding daina the bride says all her mātes radi have become strangers
phrase: 'mother's kin' as the married woman's natal family (Serb. род матере ~ Latv. mātes radi)
note: Balto-Slavic only, and 'mother's kin' is a natural expression; one Latvian witness in the corpus. Claimed only because both continue the same cognate pair for the same social referent in matching contexts.

near_miss.lead: distributive polyptoton 'from hill to hill' (Russ. с холмы на холму ~ Lat. colles collibus, *kelH-)
near_miss.why_not: Lucretius describes hills echoing to one another, the bylina the hero's horse leaping; the figure is generic distributive repetition, contexts differ

the basic technical meaning of the root; the bylina is coffin-making, Homer a list of craftsmen

near_miss.why_not: natural association, and Russian тать ночной most likely echoes the Biblical 'thief in the night' (OCS татъ въ нощи); 'night' is not cognate (aktu-)

note: second reader of the 81 flagged bundles only. Claims: 'sweet mead' (medium; Gk μέθυ ἡδύ, OE swētne medo, Ved. svādú mádhu as support, BSl. renewal *sald-) and 'mother's kin' (low, BSl. only). Many flagged bundles are repetitions of the same few stock lines.
